order: The disposable-checkout sweep deleted a live checkout mid-verification: git records resolved worktree paths, while a live checkout's handle may be spelled through a symlink (macOS /var -> /private/var) or an 8.3 short path, so the lexical live-set compare missed. Make the live-set exemption compare path identity, not string identity: resolve real paths when the path is on disk, and keep the lexical form as the fallback for registrations whose directory is gone. Pin the regression with a reproducer that stands a live checkout up under an aliased tmp root (junction on Windows, symlink elsewhere), failing on every platform without the fix and skipping where links cannot be created. The sweep's structural ownership guard is out of scope and stays as written. A registration counts as ours only when its own basename is checkout and the parent directory's own basename carries the orchestra-verifier- prefix, a structural test that must never become a substring match anywhere in the path.
claims: Path normalization resolves real paths now, with the lexical form kept as the fallback for paths already gone, so the live-set exemption holds however a live checkout's handle is spelled. The aliased-tmp-root reproducer, a junction on Windows and a symlink elsewhere, skips where links are unavailable, fails without the fix and passes with it. The structural ownership guard came through this change untouched — own basename plus the parent's own basename prefix, still structural, with no substring matching anywhere. The full suite reports 97 passed and zero failed.
